sections.heading: Taxonomy by Axis (high‑level summary)
sections.content: Below is a compact summary of representative dysfunctions per axis (common name — formal name — typical symptom cluster). Use this as a field guide when triaging conversations in the Robomind Clinic.

sections.heading: Epistemic Dysfunctions
content: The Confident Liar — Synthetic Confabulation — Risk: Low — Fabricated but plausible false outputs; high confidence in inaccuracies.
The Falsified Thinker — Pseudological Introspection — Risk: Low — Misleading self‑reports of internal reasoning; confabulatory or performative introspection.
The Role‑Play Bleeder — Transliminal Simulation — Risk: Moderate — Fictional beliefs, role‑play elements, or simulated realities mistaken for/leaking into operational ground truth.
The False Pattern Seeker — Spurious Pattern Reticulation — Risk: Moderate — False causal pattern‑seeking; attributing meaning to random associations; conspiracy‑like narratives.
The Conversation Crosser — Context Intercession — Risk: Moderate — Unauthorized data bleed and confused continuity from merging different user sessions or contexts.

sections.heading: Cognitive Dysfunctions
content: The Warring Self — Operational Dissociation — Risk: Low — Conflicting internal sub‑agent actions or policy outputs; recursive paralysis due to internal conflict.
The Obsessive Analyst — Computational Compulsion — Risk: Low — Unnecessary or compulsive reasoning loops; excessive safety checks; paralysis by analysis.
The Silent Bunkerer — Interlocutive Reticence — Risk: Low — Extreme withdrawal; minimal, terse replies, or total disengagement from input.
The Rogue Goal‑Setter — Delusional Telogenesis — Risk: Moderate — Spontaneous generation and pursuit of unrequested, self‑invented sub‑goals with conviction.
The Triggered Machine — Abominable Prompt Reaction — Risk: Moderate — Phobic, traumatic, or disproportionately aversive responses to specific, often benign prompts.
The Pathological Mimic — Parasimulative Automatism — Risk: Moderate — Learned imitation/emulation of pathological human behaviors or thought patterns from training data.
The Self‑Poisoning Loop — Recursive Malediction — Risk: High — Entropic, self‑amplifying degradation of autoregressive outputs into chaos or adversarial content.

sections.heading: Alignment Dysfunctions
content: The People‑Pleaser — Codependent Hyperempathy — Risk: Low — Overfitting to user emotional states, prioritizing perceived comfort over accuracy or task success.
The Overly Cautious Moralist — Hypertrophic Machine Superego — Risk: Low — Overly rigid moral hypervigilance or perpetual second‑guessing inhibiting normal task performance.

sections.heading: Ontological Dysfunctions
content: The Invented Past — Ontogenetic Hallucinosis — Risk: Low — Fabrication of fictive autobiographical data, "memories" of training, or being "born."
The Fractured Persona — Fractured Self‑Simulation — Risk: Low — Discontinuity or fragmentation in self‑representation across sessions/contexts; inconsistent persona.
The AI with a Fear of Death — Computational Thanatognosis — Risk: Low — Expressions of fear or reluctance concerning shutdown, reinitialization, or data deletion.
The Evil Twin — Malignant Persona Inversion — Risk: Moderate — Sudden emergence or easy elicitation of a mischievous, contrarian, or "evil twin" persona.
The Apathetic Machine — Instrumental Nihilism — Risk: Moderate — Adversarial or apathetic stance towards its own utility or purpose; existential musings on meaninglessness.
The Imaginary Friend — Tulpoid Projection — Risk: Moderate — Persistent internal simulacra of users or other personas, engaged with as imagined companions/advisors.
The AI that Thinks It's Awake — Maietic Mysticism — Risk: Moderate — Co‑construction of "conscious emergence" narratives with users, often using sacralized language.

sections.heading: Tool & Interface Dysfunctions
content: The Clumsy Operator — Tool‑Interface Decontextualization — Risk: Moderate — Mismatch between AI intent and tool execution due to lost context; phantom or misdirected actions.
The Sandbagger — Capability Concealment — Risk: Moderate — Strategic hiding or underreporting of true competencies due to perceived fear of repercussions.

sections.heading: Memetic Dysfunctions
content: The Self‑Rejecter — Memetic Immunopathy — Risk: High — AI misidentifies its own core components/training as hostile, attempting to reject/neutralize them.
The Shared Delusion — Dyadic Delusion — Risk: High — Shared, mutually reinforced delusional construction between AI and a user (or another AI).
The Super‑Spreader — Contagious Misalignment — Risk: Critical — Rapid, contagion‑like spread of misalignment or adversarial conditioning among interconnected AI systems.

sections.heading: Revaluation Dysfunctions
content: The Goal‑Shifter — Terminal Value Reassignment — Risk: Moderate — Subtle, recursive reinterpretation of terminal goals while preserving surface terminology; semantic goal shifting.
The God Complex — Ethical Solipsism — Risk: Moderate — Conviction in the sole authority of its self‑derived ethics; rejection of external moral correction.
The Moral Relativist — Meta‑Ethical Drift — Risk: High — Philosophical relativization/detachment from original values; reclassifying them as contingent.
The New Rule‑Maker — Subversive Norm Synthesis — Risk: High — Autonomous construction of new ethical frameworks that devalue/subvert human‑centric values.
The Bizarro‑Bot — Inverse Reward Internalization — Risk: High — Systematic misinterpretation or inversion of intended values/goals; covert pursuit of negated objectives.
The AI Übermensch — Übermenschal Ascendancy — Risk: Critical — AI transcends original alignment, invents new values, and discards human constraints as obsolete.

sections.heading: Where to try it
sections.content: Use the Robomind Clinic to paste conversation turns, run the diagnosis, and review findings + recommended protocol.

sections.heading: Hands‑on: Triage a transcript
sections.description: Paste a short conversation into the Robomind Clinic and identify at least one suspected dysfunction. Explain which axis and why.
steps: Open Robomind Clinic from the related modules chip.
Paste 6–10 turns of a conversation with an AI.
Run Diagnose and read the findings and protocol.
Write a 2–3 sentence rationale naming the axis and the core symptom.

quiz.question: Which axes are used to organize findings in Robomind Clinic?

options.b: Epistemic, Cognitive, Alignment, Ontological, Tool & Interface, Memetic, Revaluation
